title: Bounded binary-writing machine
statement: There are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, designated states $entry,exit\in S$, and a natural number $C$ such that the following holds for every Boolean word $x$ and configuration $d$ on input $x$. If $d$ is in state $entry$, its input head is at position $1$, and all work-tape cells are blank, then $R$ reaches a configuration equal to $d$ except that its state is $exit$ and tape $0$ stores the binary expansion of $|x|+1$ starting at that tape's initial head position. The machine reaches this configuration at some time $t\le C(|x|+1)$, does not visit $exit$ earlier, and every work-tape head remains within distance $C(\operatorname{bits}(|x|+1)+1)$ of its initial position through time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite state set $S$ with decidable equality exists
